name: Ferrogate Harbor Ferry
description: Electric catamarans running routes across the harbor and along the lakefront. Slower than the L-train but scenic and surprisingly reliable. The ferry is one of the few public transit options that doesn't feel like punishment — lake air, open deck, room to breathe. The catch: routes only serve waterfront districts, and winter icing shuts down service for three months a year.
propulsion: Electric turbine, solar-assist panels on upper deck
common_usage: Waterfront commuters, Old Harbor workers, tourists. The only pleasant public transit experience in GLMZ.
story_hooks: A ferry captain reports seeing lights moving under the water — organized, deliberate, following the hull
The winter ferry shutdown creates a three-month isolation for island communities that someone is exploiting
